text: Do not sacrifice to the LORD your God an ox or a sheep that has any defect or serious flaw, for that is detestable to the LORD your God.
If a man or woman among you, in one of the towns the LORD your God is giving you, is found doing what is evil in the eyes of the LORD your God, violating his covenant,
and has gone and served other gods and bowed down to them, or to the sun or the moon or any of the host of heaven—something I never commanded—
and if it is reported to you and you hear of it, then investigate the matter thoroughly. If it is true and confirmed that such a detestable thing has been done in Israel,
then bring out to your gates the man or the woman who has done this evil thing, and stone that man or woman to death.
On the testimony of two or three witnesses a person shall be put to death; no one shall be put to death on the testimony of only one witness.
The hands of the witnesses shall be the first raised against him to put him to death, and afterward the hands of all the people. So you shall purge the evil from among you.
If a case is too difficult for you to judge—cases of bloodshed, of legal rights, or of bodily injury—any dispute within your towns, then rise and go up to the place the LORD your God will choose.

versions.text: If a case is too difficult for you to judge—whether bloodshed, lawsuits, or assaults—any dispute within your towns, then go up to the place the LORD your God will choose.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew idiom "between blood and blood, between claim and claim, between injury and injury" refers to distinguishing between types of cases; "cases of..." carries this better than a bare list. Also, וְקַמְתָּ ("you shall arise") is not represented; "rise and go up" restores it and improves the rhythm of the clause.

text: Go to the Levitical priests and to the judge who is in office at that time. Bring your inquiry to them, and they will give you the verdict.
You must act according to the decision they give you from that place the LORD will choose. Be careful to do everything they instruct you.

versions.text: You must act according to the decision they give you at the place the LORD will choose. Be careful to do everything they instruct you.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has מִן ("from that place"), stressing that the ruling issues from the chosen sanctuary; "at the place" weakens this and slightly shifts the sense.

versions.text: You must act according to the decision they give you from that place the LORD will choose.
versions.explanation: The second clause of the Hebrew verse (וְשָׁמַרְתָּ לַעֲשׂוֹת כְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר יוֹרוּךָ, "and you shall be careful to do according to all that they instruct you") has been dropped. The earlier revision included it; restoring it keeps the whole verse while preserving the intentional "from that place" rendering.

text: Act according to the instruction they give you and the judgment they declare to you. Do not turn aside from what they tell you, to the right or to the left.
Anyone who acts arrogantly and refuses to listen to the priest who ministers there before the LORD your God, or to the judge, must die. So you shall purge the evil from Israel.
Then all the people will hear and be afraid, and will not act arrogantly again.
When you enter the land the LORD your God is giving you and take possession of it and settle in it, and you say, "Let us set a king over us like all the nations around us,"
be sure to set over you the king the LORD your God chooses. He must come from among your own brothers. You may not place a foreigner over you, one who is not your brother.

versions.text: be sure to set over you the king the LORD your God chooses. He must be one of your own people. You may not place a foreigner over you, someone who is not your brother.
versions.explanation: The verse builds a deliberate contrast on the same word אָח ("brother"): from among your brothers / not your brother. Rendering the first instance as "your own people" and the second as "your brother" obscures the parallel; using "brothers" in both places preserves the echo and reads well aloud.

text: He must not acquire great numbers of horses for himself, or send the people back to Egypt to get more of them, for the LORD has told you, "You are never to return that way again."
He must not take many wives, or his heart will be led astray. And he must not accumulate great amounts of silver and gold.
When he takes the throne of his kingdom, he is to write for himself on a scroll a copy of this law, copied from the scroll kept by the Levitical priests.

versions.text: When he takes the throne of his kingdom, he is to write for himself a copy of this law on a scroll, taken from that of the Levitical priests.
versions.explanation: "Taken from that of the Levitical priests" is vague and stumbles when read aloud, since "that" has no clear antecedent. Naming the scroll makes the sense of מִלִּפְנֵי (from the copy in the priests' keeping) explicit and flows better orally.

text: He is to keep it with him and read it all the days of his life, so that he may learn to fear the LORD his God and keep all the words of this law and these statutes, and do them—

so that his heart may not be lifted up above his brothers, and he may not turn from the commandment to the right or to the left, and so that he and his descendants may reign long over his kingdom in Israel.
